acceptance.run.description: run the specification's conformance suite against the release; only while no run is recorded about the current release revision against the current specification revision

release.build.description: build a release revision from the merged changes

spec.gate.description: run the ESS gate over the current specification revision; only while no gate run is recorded about it: a second record with another result would leave gate.passed unknown for good

release.description: the versioned, deployable unit built from the merged changes

spec.description: the ESS specification; its revision is its spec digest, as in the parent case

gate.checked.description: an ESS gate run is recorded about the current specification revision, whatever its result

gate.passed.description: the ESS gate passes on the current specification revision

release.acceptance_run.description: a conformance run is recorded about the current release revision, against the current specification revision, whatever its result

release.accepted.description: the conformance suite of the current specification passes on the current release

release.built.description: the current release revision carries build provenance

build_provenance.description: the record of how a release revision was built from the merged changes

ess_gate.description: the ESS gate over a specification revision, the four checks run as one program; passed or failed

release_conformance.description: `ess verify conform run --target <release> --strict` of the specification's suite against a release revision; its result is passed, failed or inconclusive

spec.revised.description: a conformance run observed against an earlier specification revision no longer applies

acceptance.required.description: the conformance suite passes on the release

gate.required.description: the ESS gate passes on the current specification revision

not_accepted.description: the conformance suite failed (or was inconclusive) on the current release revision. Nothing in this case changes the merged changes, so a rebuild gives the same release and the same result; the case ends here, the epic ends not_accepted and the root not_delivered

passed.description: delivered: the ESS gate passes, and the current release is built and accepted by the conformance suite of the current specification revision

protocol.description: Prove that an epic whose stories are merged is delivered and tested, the last stage of the development cycle: build the merged changes into a release revision with provenance, then run the ESS conformance suite of the current specification revision against it. The ESS gate must pass on the current specification revision. A revised specification invalidates the conformance runs observed against the earlier revision. Delivery is derived from the checks, with no approval: the case ends passed (delivered) once the gate passes and the release is built and accepted, and not_accepted, without a person, once the acceptance run failed on the current release revision (no action of this case reworks the merged changes; the stories did). Publishing, observing and rolling back are sdc.release, which nothing in the cycle opens.
